about: The upstream's agents the driver runs, by the agent option: each its own script at the tested commit, as published, on one task. argv is what its scripts/bash wrapper passes (run_multienv_m3.sh, run_multienv_muse_spark.sh), less what Nullius sets for every unit (common: the docker provider, the VM image, one environment, the image's password as the wrapper passes it, the task's meta file, the unit's results) and less the aws provider's --region and --use_public_ip and the wrapper's one --specific_task_id. M3 also gets the relay's key as --api_key, since its script reads MINIMAX_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and MINIMAX_API_KEY before ANTHROPIC_*, and a .env file in the upstream (each script calls load_dotenv) could set them. Muse Spark gets the reasoning effort and output budget of its published run's args.json (max, 262144) in place of its wrapper's (high, 8192), and MUSE_SPARK_SKIP_INPUT_TOKEN_PREFLIGHT, since its count of input tokens before each call asks the endpoint for a path OpenRouter does not serve. env points each script's model client at the unit's relay too, and its simulated user's, asked by the name the documented invocation gives it (OSWORLD_USER_SIM_MODEL), which the Original setup sends on as a side model. {model} is the model asked, {base_url} the unit's relay (ending /v1), {base} the same without /v1 (the Anthropic client adds /v1/messages), {key} the relay's placeholder, {vm} the VM image, {up} the upstream, {meta} the unit's task file, {results} the unit's results folder, {examples} the upstream's evaluation_examples. --max_steps is each wrapper's own, unless the max_steps option sets another. models are the ones each agent is published with, by the names its code knows; model_argv adds what its documented invocation passes for one of them.
